It is located in {{ill|Chikuzen Province|cs|Provincie Čikuzen|de|Provinz Chikuzen|es|Provincia de Chikuzen|fa|ولایت چیکوزن|fr|Chikuzen|gl|Provincia de Chikuzen|id|Provinsi Chikuzen|it|Chikuzen (provincia)|ja|筑前国|ko|지쿠젠국|lt|Čikudzeno žemė|nl|Chikuzen (provincie)|no|Chikuzen (provins)|pt|Província de Chikuzen|ru|Тикудзэн (провинция)|simple|Chikuzen Province|sk|Čikuzen (provincia)|sr|Провинција Чикузен|tr|Chikuzen (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Тікудзен|zh|筑前國|zh_min_nan|Tikuzen-kok|zh_yue|筑前國|qid=Q1047664|lt=Chikuzen Province}}.

It claims to be the head shrine of all {{ill|Watatsumi shrines|ja|綿津見神社|qid=Q11607434}} and {{ill|Watatsumi Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|海神社|qid=Q123530063}} nationwide<ref name="由緒書"/>. It is praised as the “capital of dragons” and is known as a place associated with the ancient clan {{ill|Azumi people|fr|Peuple Azumi|id|Suku Azumi|it|Azumi (popolo)|ja|阿曇氏|ko|아즈미씨|ru|Адзуми (народ)|simple|Azumi people|qid=Q3377806}} (also written Adzumi).

== Shrine name ==
Regarding the origin of the word “Shika” (志賀), which is also the island name of {{ill|Shika Island|fa|شیکانوشیما|fr|Shikano-shima|ja|志賀島|ko|시카노섬|simple|Shika Island|zh|志賀島|qid=Q3077260}}, an excerpt from the *Chikuzen no Kuni Fudoki* <ref group="原">Excerpt from the *Chikuzen no Kuni Fudoki* cited in *Shaku Nihongi*, vol. 6, section on the deities worshiped by the Azumi no Muraji, etc.</ref> says that, based on a tradition connected to {{ill|Empress Jingū|ar|الإمبراطورة جينغو|arz|الامبراطوره جينجو|az|Cinqu|bcl|Empress Jingū|ca|Jingu|cs|Džingú|de|Jingū|es|Jingū|eu|Jingū enperatriza|fa|امپراتریس (държава)|bs|Kraljevstvo Sila|ca|Silla (Corea)|cdo|Sĭng-lò̤|ckb|شیللا|cs|Silla|da|Silla (koreansk stat)|de|Silla|eo|Silla|es|Silla (Corea)|eu|Silla (Korea)|fa|پادشاهی شیلا|fi|Silla|fr|Silla the area was called “Chikashima (近島, ‘near island’),” which later shifted in pronunciation to “Shikashima (資珂島)” <ref name="地名"/>.  

The shrine name “Shikaumi” (志賀海) is now pronounced “Shikaumi,” but as for the original pronunciation there are various theories such as “Shika no Wata,” “Shika no Ama,” “Shika no Umi,” and “Shika ni Imasu Wata,” among others <ref name="神々"/>.  

== Enshrined deities ==
The deities are enshrined as follows: one principal deity in each of the left, center, and right halls, along with one associated deity in each hall <ref name="由緒書"/>. The three principal deities are collectively called the “{{ill|Watatsumi|abstract|Q1474187|az|Vatatsumi|de|Watatsumi|es|Watatsumi|fa|واتاتسومی|fr|Watatsumi|hu|Vatacumi|ja|ワタツミ|ko|와타쓰미|mni|ꯋꯇꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|pl|Watatsumi|ru|Ватацуми|simple|Watatsumi|uk|Вататсумі|zh|綿津見|qid=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi Three Deities}}” (綿津見三神, watatsumi sanshin) <ref name="由緒書"/>.  
* Left Hall: **Nakatsu Watatsumi no Kami** (仲津綿津見神)  
** Associated deity of the Left Hall: {{ill|Empress Jingū|ar|الإمبراطورة جينغو|arz|الامبراطوره جينجو|az|Cinqu|bcl|Empress Jingū|ca|Jingu|cs|Džingú|de|Jingū|es|Jingū|eu|Jingū enperatriza|fa|امپراتریس جینگو|fr|Jingū|hr|Jingū (japanska carica)|hu|Dzsingú japán császárnő|id|Permaisuri Jingū|it|Jingū|ja|神功皇后|ka|ძინგუ|ko|진구 황후|nl|Jingu|pl|Jingū|pt|Jingu|ru|Императрица Дзингу|sh|Carica Jingū|si|ජින්ගූ අධිරාජිනිය|simple|Empress Jingū|sl|Cesarica Džingu|sv|Jingu Kogo|te|రాణి జింగూ|th|จักรพรรดินีจิงงู|tl|Emperatris Jingū|tr|Jingū (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператриця Дзінґу|uz|Imperator Jingū|vi|Thiên hoàng Jingū|zh|神功皇后|zh_min_nan|Sîn-kong Hông-hō͘|zh_yue|神功皇后|qid=Q232803}} (神功皇后)  
* Center Hall: **Sokotsu Watatsumi no Kami** (底津綿津見神)  
** Associated deity of the Center Hall: {{ill|Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|fa|تامایوری-هیمه|fr|Tamayori-bime|it|Tamayori-hime|ja|タマヨリビメ (日向神話)|mni|ꯇꯃꯌꯣꯔꯤ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Tamayori-bime|ru|Тамаёри-химэ|uk|Тамайорі хіме но мікото|zh|玉依姬|qid=Q3082751|lt=Princess Tamayorihime}} (玉依姫命)  
* Right Hall: **Uwatsu Watatsumi no Kami** (表津綿津見神)   
** Associated deity of the Right Hall: {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997}} (応神天皇)  

== About the enshrined deities ==
The three Watatsumi (sea / Watatsumi / Watatsumi of the “少童” reading) deities are regarded as sea gods, as seen in the ancient name for the sea “Wata / Watanohara” (“sea = wata, watanohara”) <ref>“Kaijin Shinkō” entry, *Kokushi Daijiten*.</ref>. In the “birth of the gods” section of the {{ill|Kojiki|ace|Kojiki|ar|كوجيكي|az|Kociki|bcl|Kojiki|be|Кодзікі|bg|Коджики|ca|Kojiki|ckb|کۆجیکی|cs|Kodžiki|da|Kojiki|de|Kojiki|eo|Koĝiki|es|Kojiki|et|Kojiki|eu|Kojiki|fa|کوجیکی|fi|Kojiki|fr|Kojiki|gl|Kojiki|he|קוג'יקי|hi|कोजिकी|hr|Kojiki|hu|Kodzsiki|hy|Կոձիկի|id|Kojiki|it|Kojiki|ja|古事記|ka|კოძიკი|kk|Кодзики|kn|ಕೋಜಿಕಿ|ko|고사기|la|Kojiki|lt|Kodžiki|mk|Коџики|ml|കൊജികി|ms|Kojiki|my|ခိုဂျိခိ|nl|Kojiki|no|Kojiki|oc|Kojiki|pl|Kojiki|pt|Kojiki|ro|Kojiki|rsk|Кодїки|ru|Кодзики|sh|Kojiki|simple|Kojiki|sk|Kodžiki|sl|Kodžiki|sr|Коџики|sv|Kojiki|ta|கோஜிகி|th|โคจิกิ|tl|Kojiki|tr|Kojiki|uk|Кодзікі|vi|Cổ sự ký|zh|古事記|zh_classical|古事記|qid=Q813031}} and {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}}, during the purification rite ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=misogi}}), they are described as gods born together with the {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|de|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|it|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|ja|住吉三神|mni|ꯁꯨꯃꯤꯌꯣꯁꯤ ꯁꯟꯖꯤꯟ|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနတ်သုံးပါး|pl|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|simple|Sumiyoshi sanjin|zh|住吉三神|qid=Q1114013}} as follows.  
* *Kojiki*  
*: It calls the three born deities—Sokotsu Watatsumi no Kami, Nakatsu Watatsumi no Kami, and Uwatsu Watatsumi no Kami—collectively “Watatsumi no Kami,” and states, “They are the gods whom the Azumi no Muraji (あずみのむらじ) and others venerate as their ancestral deity” <ref name="綿津見神"/>.  
* *Nihon Shoki*  
*: After saying, “The sea gods born were named Sukunahiko no Mikoto,” it records that the three born deities—Sokotsu Sukunahiko no Mikoto, Nakatsu Sukunahiko no Mikoto, and Uwatsu Sukunahiko no Mikoto—are “the gods whom the Azumi no Muraji and others worship” <ref name="綿津見神"/>.  

Thus, in the *Kojiki* and *Nihon Shoki*, the Watatsumi Three Deities are treated as the ancestral gods or worshiped gods of the **{{ill|Azumi people|fr|Peuple Azumi|id|Suku Azumi|it|Azumi (popolo)|ja|阿曇氏|ko|아즈미씨|ru|Адзуми (народ)|simple|Azumi people|qid=Q3377806}}** (Azumi-uji/Azumi-uji; also written 安曇氏, 阿曇族, 安曇族) <ref name="地名"/>. The reading “Azumi/Azumi” is also seen as an abbreviation of “Amatsumi (海津見),” and the Azumi clan who served these deities were a *tomonomiyatsuko* clan that oversaw groups of seafaring people <ref name="綿津見神">“Watatsumi no Kami” entry, *Kokushi Daijiten*.</ref>.  

In the {{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751}} <ref group="原">*Sendai Kujihongi*, “Onmyō Hongi” (see [{{NDLDC|991097/110}} *Kokushi Taikei*, vol. 7] (Keizai Zasshisha, 1897–1901; National Diet Library Digital Collection), frame 110).</ref>, likewise in the section on the birth of the gods, it says: “The three Sukunahiko deities are worshiped by the Azumi no Muraji and others; they are the Tsukushi Shika gods,” <ref name="神々"/> and Shikaumi Shrine is named as a clan deity under the title “Tsukushi Shika no Kami (筑紫斯香神)” <ref name="神々"/>.  

As other major sea gods besides Watatsumi, Sumiyoshi ({{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|de|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|it|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|ja|住吉三神|mni|ꯁꯨꯃꯤꯌꯣꯁꯤ ꯁꯟꯖꯤꯟ|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနတ်သုံးပါး|pl|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|simple|Sumiyoshi sanjin|zh|住吉三神|qid=Q1114013}}; worshiped by the Sumiyoshi clan) and Munakata ({{ill|Three Munakata Goddesses|ja|宗像三女神|ko|무나카타 삼여신|simple|Three Munakata goddesses|zh|宗像三女神|qid=Q10948069}}; worshiped by the {{ill|Munakata clan|fr|Clan Munakata|ja|宗像氏|simple|Munakata clan|qid=Q16481907|lt=Munakata lineage}}) are well known, and in northern Kyūshū there are shrines dedicated to each: {{ill|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)|abstract|Q29682|de|Sumiyoshi-Schrein (Fukuoka)|fr|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)|ja|住吉神社 (福岡市)|simple|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)|zh|住吉神社 (福岡市)|qid=Q29682|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} and {{ill|Munakata Taisha|abstract|Q704962|fr|Munakata-taisha|it|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|ka|მუნაკატა-ტაიშა|la|Munakata Taisha|lt|Munakatos maldykla|ru|Мунаката-тайся|simple|Munakata Taisha|tr|Munakata Taisha|zh|宗像大社|qid=Q704962}}.  

== History ==
[[File:Shikanoshima Island, enkei.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|{{ill|Shika Island|fa|شیکانوشیما|fr|Shikano-shima|ja|志賀島|ko|시카노섬|simple|Shika Island|zh|志賀島|qid=Q3077260}}, where Shikaumi Shrine is located}}]]  

== Founding ==
The founding date is unknown <ref name="由緒書"/>. According to shrine tradition, in ancient times it consisted of three shrines on Katsuma Beach on the north side of {{ill|Shika Island|fa|شیکانوشیما|fr|Shikano-shima|ja|志賀島|ko|시카노섬|simple|Shika Island|zh|志賀島|qid=Q3077260}}: Uwatsu-gū, Nakatsu-gū, and Okitsu-gū; but {{ill|Azumi-no-isora|it|Azumi-no-isora|ja|阿曇磯良|ko|아즈미노이소라|mni|ꯑꯓꯨꯃꯤ-ꯅꯣ-ꯏꯁꯣꯔ|ru|Адзуми-но Исора|zh|阿曇磯良|qid=Q1755974}} (Azumi no Isora: ancestor of the {{ill|Azumi people|fr|Peuple Azumi|id|Suku Azumi|it|Azumi (popolo)|ja|阿曇氏|ko|아즈미씨|ru|Адзуми (народ)|simple|Azumi people|qid=Q3377806}}) relocated the Uwatsu-gū to the south side of Shikanoshima, making it the present precinct <ref name="由緒書"/>. Nakatsu-gū and Okitsu-gū are now subordinate shrines <ref name="由緒書"/>. Azumi no Isora is also said to have served as helmsman in {{ill|Empress Jingū|ar|الإمبراطورة جينغو|arz|الامبراطوره جينجو|az|Cinqu|bcl|Empress Jingū|ca|Jingu|cs|Džingú|de|Jingū|es|Jingū|eu|Jingū enperatriza|fa|امپراتریس جینگو|fr|Jingū|hr|Jingū (japanska carica)|hu|Dzsingú japán császárnő|id|Permaisuri Jingū|it|Jingū|ja|神功皇后|ka|ძინგუ|ko|진구 황후|nl|Jingu|pl|Jingū|pt|Jingu|ru|Императрица Дзингу|sh|Carica Jingū|si|ජින්ගූ අධිරාජිනිය|simple|Empress Jingū|sl|Cesarica Džingu|sv|Jingu Kogo|te|రాణి జింగూ|th|จักรพรรดินีจิงงู|tl|Emperatris Jingū|tr|Jingū (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператриця Дзінґу|uz|Imperator Jingū|vi|Thiên hoàng Jingū|zh|神功皇后|zh_min_nan|Sîn-kong Hông-hō͘|zh_yue|神功皇后|qid=Q232803}}’s expedition to {{ill|Silla|ar|مملكة شلا|ast|Silla (Corea)|az|Şila krallığı|azb|شیلا|bar|Silla|be|Сіла (дзяржава)|bg|Сила (държава)|bs|Kraljevstvo Sila|ca|Silla (Corea)|cdo|Sĭng-lò̤|ckb|شیللا|cs|Silla|da|Silla (koreansk stat)|de|Silla|eo|Silla|es|Silla (Corea)|eu|Silla (Korea)|fa|پادشاهی شیلا|fi|Silla|fr|Silla (Corée)|gl|Reino de Silla|hi|सिल्ला|hr|Kraljevstvo Sila|hu|Silla (ókori királyság)|id|Silla|it|Silla (Corea)|ja|新羅|ka|სილა|kk|Силла|km|ស៊ីលឡា|ko|신라|ks|سِللا سَلطَنَت|ku|Keyaniya Sillayê|lt|Šila (Korėja)|lv|Silla|mk|Сила (држава)|ml|സില്ല|mn|Шилла|ms|Silla|my|ရှီလာ|mzn|سیلا|nds|Silla|nl|Silla (Korea)|no|Silla|oc|Silla (reialme)|pl|Silla|pt|Silla (Coreia)|ro|Silla|ru|Силла|sco|Silla|sh|Sila (kraljevina)|si|සිල්ලා|simple|Silla|sk|Silla|sr|Сила (краљевство)|sv|Silla|sw|Silla|th|ชิลลา|tl|Silla|tr|Silla|uk|Сілла|vi|Tân La|wuu|新罗|zh|新罗|zh_classical|新羅|zh_min_nan|Sin-lô|zh_yue|新羅|qid=Q28456}} <ref name="由緒書"/><ref name="神々"/>.  

In ancient northern Kyūshū, the {{ill|Azumi people|fr|Peuple Azumi|id|Suku Azumi|it|Azumi (popolo)|ja|阿曇氏|ko|아즈미씨|ru|Адзуми (народ)|simple|Azumi people|qid=Q3377806}} (also written 安曇氏), who governed sea people ({{ill|Ama (diving)|ca|Ama (busseig)|cs|Ama|de|Ama (Taucher)|el|Άμα|es|Ama (Japón)|et|Ama (sukelduja)|eu|Ama (urpekariak)|fi|Amat|fr|Ama (plongeuse)|hu|Ama búvárok|hy|Ամա (սուզորդ)|id|Ama (penyelam)|it|Ama (pescatrici subacquee)|ja|海人|ko|아마 (잠수부)|lt|Ama|lv|Ama|nl|Ama (duiker)|pl|Ama (nurek)|pt|Ama (Japão)|ro|Ama (scufundare)|ru|Ама (ныряльщица)|sr|Ама|sv|Ama (dykare)|th|อามะ (นักดำน้ำ)|tr|Ama (dalgıç)|uk|Ама (пірнальник)|vi|Kaijin|zh|海人 (职业)|qid=Q1577970}}), are said to have controlled maritime routes <ref name="角川"/>. Shikanoshima was a key point for sea traffic, and the area including Shikanoshima and {{ill|Umi no Nakamichi|ceb|Uminonakamichi|fr|Umino Nakamichi|ja|海の中道|ko|우미노나카미치|zh|海之中道|qid=Q2404998}} <ref group="注">Considered the area of Shika-gō and Azumi-gō in Kasuya District of Chikuzen Province as seen in the *Wamyōshō* (from the *Dictionary of Personal Names of Ancient Japanese Clans*, entry on the Azumi clan). Shika-gō is identified with Shikanoshima; Azumi-gō is identified with the area from Kamiwajiro and Shimowajiro in Higashi Ward, Fukuoka City to Shingū Town in Kasuya District, or with Shikanoshima (from *Place Names of Fukuoka Prefecture*, entries on Shika-gō and Azumi-gō).</ref> is said to have been the Azumi clan’s home base <ref name="角川">*Kadokawa Nihon Chimei Daijiten*, entry on Shikaumi Shrine.</ref>, and Shikaumi Shrine is thought to have been the clan’s central shrine <ref name="地名"/>. Even today, all of Shikanoshima is regarded as a sacred precinct <ref>*Kadokawa Nihon Chimei Daijiten*, entry on Shikanoshima.</ref>, and the current priestly family also claims descent from the Azumi clan <ref name="角川"/>. The Azumi clan is said to have expanded throughout Japan, and place names such as “Shika” and “Atsumi”—for example {{ill|Azumino|ar|أزومينو (ناغانو)|azb|آزومینو، Shikanoshima is also known for the discovery of the gold seal ({{ill|King of Na gold seal|fr|Sceau du roi de Na|id|Segel emas Raja Na|ja|漢委奴国王印|ko|한위노국왕인|ru|Печать ханского вана японской страны На|simple|King of Na gold seal|uk|Печатка вана японської країни На|zh|汉委奴国王印|qid=Q2975212}}), but it is unclear why the seal of {{ill|Nakoku|de|Na (Staat)|fr|Nakoku|it|Nakoku|ja|奴国|ko|나노국|pt|Nakoku|ru|Страна На|th|ประเทศนะ|uk|Країна На|zh|奴国|qid=Q600473}} was found there. Some theories speculate a connection between the Azumi clan—and by extension Shikaumi Shrine as their clan deity—and Na, and at Najima Shrine in Najima, Higashi Ward, Fukuoka City, the Azumi clan is regarded as the “Nake-nushi” <ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://lunabura.exblog.jp/14132415/|title=Najima Shrine|accessdate=April 13, 2010|publisher=Ayasugi Luna}}</ref>.

== Precincts ==
[[File:Shikaumi-jinja shaden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Worship hall (front) and main sanctuary (rear right)}}]]  
The precinct is located on the south side of Shikanoshima. It is said that Shikaumi Shrine was formerly on the north side of Shikanoshima and consisted of three shrines—Uwatsu-gū, Nakatsu-gū, and Okitsu-gū <ref name="由緒書"/>. Of these, Uwatsu-gū was transferred here and became the present main shrine, while Nakatsu-gū and Okitsu-gū are now subordinate shrines. The former site of Uwatsu-gū is said to be in Katsuma, Higashi Ward, Fukuoka City ({{Coord|33|41|13.00|N|130|17|32.74|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|name=Site of Uwatsu-gū (former location)}}).  

In the precinct’s Rokkakudō (鹿角堂), many deer antlers—said to number over ten thousand—have been dedicated. There is also a sacred stone dedicated in later times called the “Kameishi (亀石, ‘turtle stone’),” linked to a tradition that during {{ill|Empress Jingū|ar|الإمبراطورة جينغو|arz|الامبراطوره جينجو|az|Cinqu|bcl|Empress Jingū|ca|Jingu|cs|Džingú|de|Jingū|es|Jingū|eu|Jingū enperatriza|fa|امپراتریس جینگو|fr|Jingū|hr|Jingū (japanska carica)|hu|Dzsingú japán császárnő|id|Permaisuri Jingū|it|Jingū|ja|神功皇后|ka|ძინგუ|ko|진구 황후|nl|Jingu|pl|Jingū|pt|Jingu|ru|Императрица Дзингу|sh|Carica Jingū|si|ජින්ගූ අධිරාජිනිය|simple|Empress Jingū|sl|Cesarica Džingu|sv|Jingu Kogo|te|రాణి జింగూ|th|จักรพรรดินีจิงงู|tl|Emperatris Jingū|tr|Jingū (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператриця Дзінґу|uz|Imperator Jingū|vi|Thiên hoàng Jingū|zh|神功皇后|zh_min_nan|Sîn-kong Hông-hō͘|zh_yue|神功皇后|qid=Q232803}}’s {{ill|Three Han Campaign|ja|三韓征伐|ko|삼한 정벌|zh|三韩征伐|qid=Q11249435}}, {{ill|Azumi-no-isora|it|Azumi-no-isora|ja|阿曇磯良|ko|아즈미노이소라|mni|ꯑꯓꯨꯃꯤ-ꯅꯣ-ꯏꯁꯣꯔ|ru|Адзуми-но Исора|zh|阿曇磯良|qid=Q1755974}} appeared before the empress riding a turtle <ref name="神々"/>.  

Along the approach stands a stone *Hōkyōintō* pagoda. A {{ill|Hōkyōintō|es|Hōkyōintō|fa|هوکیواینتو|fr|Hōkyōintō|it|Hōkyōintō|ja|宝篋印塔|ko|보협인탑|nl|Hōkyōintō|zh|宝箧印式塔|qid=Q3146365}} is a pagoda that enshrines a Buddhist scripture (the *Hōkyōin Dharani Sutra*) <ref name="説明板">Explanatory signboard in the precinct.</ref>. == Auxiliary shrines (sessha and massha) ==
There are a total of 24 auxiliary shrines: 5 sessha and 19 massha <ref name="由緒書">Shrine origin pamphlet. </ref>. According to the *Chikuzen no Kuni Zoku Fudoki*, there were once 375 massha, but they were damaged in the Warring States turmoil; at the time of restoration by {{ill|Mochiyo Ōuchi|ja|大内持世|ko|오우치 모치요|qid=Q11432525}} in {{ill|Eikyō|fa|ایکیو (دوره موروماچی)|fr|Ère Eikyō|ja|永享|ko|에이쿄|ru|Эйкё|simple|Eikyō|sr|Еикјо|sv|Eikyō|tr|Eikyō|uk|Ейкьо|zh|永享|qid=Q1193059}} 11 ({{ill|1439|ab|1439|af|1439|als|1439|am|1439 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1439|ar|1439|ary|1439|arz|1439|ast|1439|avk|1439|az|1439|azb|۱۴۳۹ (میلادی)|be|1439|be_x_old|1439|bg|1439|bn|১৪৩৯|bpy|মারি ১৪৩৯|br|1439|bs|1439.|ca|1439|cdo|1439 nièng|ceb|1439|ckb|١٤٣٩|crh|1439|cs|1439|csb|1439|cv|1439|cy|1439|da|1439|de|1439|diq|1439|el|1439|eml|1439|eo|1439|es|1439|et|1439|eu|1439|fa|۱۴۳۹ (میلادی)|fi|1439|fo|1439|fr|1439|frr|1439|fy|1439|ga|1439|gan|1439年|gcr|1439|gd|1439|gl|1439|he|1439|hi|१४३९|hr|1439.|ht|1439 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1439|hy|1439|ia|1439|id|1439|ilo|1439|io|1439|is|1439|it|1439|ja|1439年|jv|1439|ka|1439|kaa|1439|kk|1439 жыл|ko|1439년|la|1439|lb|1439|li|1439|lij|1439|lmo|1439|lt|1439 m.|lv|1439. gads|mai|१४३९|map_bms|1439|mdf|1439|mhr|1439|mi|1439|min|1439|mk|1439|mr|इ.स. १४३९|mrj|1439 и|ms|1439|my|၁၄၃၉|mzn|۱۴۳۹|nah|1439|nap|1439|nds|1439|nds_nl|1439|new|सन् १४३९|nl|1439|nn|1439|no|1439|nrm|1439|nso|1439|oc|1439|or|୧୪୩୯|os|1439-æм аз|pl|1439|pnb|1439|pt|1439|qu|1439|ro|1439|ru|1439 год|rue|1439|sa|१४३९|sah|1439|scn|1439|sd|1439ع|se|1439|sh|1439.|shn|1439|sk|1439|sl|1439|smn|1439|sq|1439|sr|1439|su|1439|sv|1439|sw|1439|ta|1439|tg|Соли 1439|th|พ.ศ. 1982|tk|1439|tl|1439|tly|1439|tr|1439|tt|1439 ел|uk|1439|ur|1439ء|uz|1439|vec|1439|vi|1439|vls|1439|wa|1439|war|1439|wuu|1439年|xmf|1439|zh|1439年|zh_min_nan|1439 nî|zh_yue|1439年|qid=Q6380}}), there were a little over 120, and later in the Edo period there were only about five <ref name="神々"/>.

== Massha ==
There are 19 massha in total: 12 in Shika, 5 in Katsuma, 1 in Hiro, and 1 in Ōtake <ref name="由緒書"/>.

</gallery>  

== Festivals ==
== Annual grand festival ==
Shikaumi Shrine’s annual grand festival is called the “Kunchi Festival” (国土祭). On the previous day, every other year (odd-numbered years in the Western calendar), the shrine’s largest festival, the “Goshinkō Festival” (御神幸祭), is held <ref name="神幸"/>. In the past it was held on the old lunar calendar: September 8 (Goshinkō Festival) and September 9 (Kunchi Festival), but today it is held on {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Health and Sports Day}} and the day before (the second Monday of October and the preceding day) <ref name="神幸"/>.  

Before the festival, on lunar September 1 (October 1), a “Otokoyama Festival” is held in which a {{ill|demarchy|bg|Демархия|ca|Demarquia|cs|Demarchie|de|Demarchie|es|Demarquía|eu|Demarkia|fa|دمارشی|fi|Demarkia|hy|Դեմարխիա|ja|くじ|nl|Demarchie|oc|Demarquia|pt|Demarquia|ru|Демархия|sh|Ždrijeb (izbori)|simple|Demarchy|tl|Demarkiya|tr|Demarşi|uk|Демархія|xmf|დემარქია|qid=Q5433694}} determines whether to conduct the procession (today it is held biennially) <ref name="神幸"/>. In the Goshinkō Festival, beginning at 9 p.m. on the night of lunar September 8 (the night before Health and Sports Day), three mikoshi (Ichinoto, Ninoto, Sannotō) depart and proceed to a temporary shrine (tonomiya) <ref name="神幸"/>. There, performances based on the shrine’s origin traditions—such as the “Dragon Dance,” “Yaotome Dance,” and “Kakko Dance”—are dedicated <ref name="神幸"/>. The mikoshi then return to the shrine, the spirit is transferred back to the main sanctuary, and the Goshinkō Festival ends <ref name="神幸"/>. On the following day, lunar September 9 (Health and Sports Day), *yabusame* ({{ill|Yabusame|ar|يابوسامه|az|Yabusame|da|Yabusame|de|Yabusame|es|Yabusame|fa|یابوسامه|fr|Yabusame|it|Yabusame|ja|流鏑馬|ko|야부사메|pl|Yabusame|ru|Ябусамэ|simple|Yabusame|sv|Yabusame|tr|Yabusame|uk|Ябусаме|zh|流鏑馬|zh_classical|流鏑馬|qid=Q1886157}}) is offered <ref name="神幸"/>.  

Because it involves moving the divine spirit at night and aims to reaffirm the tradition for the people through performances rooted in the shrine’s origin narrative, the Goshinkō Festival is said to preserve an ancient form <ref name="神幸"/>. The rites are designated a Fukuoka Prefecture intangible folk cultural property as the “Shikaumi Shrine Shinkō Event” <ref name="神幸"/>.  

== Special rites ==
; Hosha Festival  
: “Hosha-sai.” A New Year rite held among annual events from January 2 to 15, conducted on a Sunday near January 15 <ref name="歩射"/>. In the past, Hosha was held on January 15 <ref name="歩射"/>. “Hosha,” i.e., shooting a {{ill|Bow and arrow|ar|قوس وسهم|bn|তীর-ধনুক|ckb|تیروکەوان|cy|Bwa saeth|da|Bue og pil|de|Pfeilbogen|dga|Tambo ane tampii|eo|Pafarko kaj sago|es|Arco y flecha|fa|تیر و کمان|fr|Arc et flèche|gd|Bogha is saighead|gn|Guyrapa|he|חץ וקשת|hi|धनुष और तीर|id|Busur panah|ja|弓矢|jam|Bou ah haro|kcg|A̱ta|km|ដងធ្នូ|kn|ಬಿಲ್ಲು ಮತ್ತು ಬಾಣ|ko|궁시|ks|تیٖر کَمان|mg|Tsipìka (fitaovana)|mr|धनुष्य व बाण|ne|धनुष बाण|nn|Pil og boge|pt|Arco e flecha|sd|تير ڪمان|so|Leeb iyo qaanso|sq|Harku dhe shigjeta|sr|Лук и стријела|su|Panah|ta|வில்–அம்பு|te|విల్లు - బాణం|tr|Yay ve ok|uk|Лук і стріли|zh|弓箭|zh_yue|弓箭|zu|Umnsalo nomcibisholo|qid=Q19827042|lt=bow}} on foot (not on horseback), is a Shinto rite for warding off evil and divining the year’s fortunes <ref name="歩射"/>. It is connected to a tradition of Azumi Momotari (百足) slaying an earth spider (tsuchigumo) <ref name="歩射"/>.  
: In Hosha, young men chosen from parishioners serve as archers and shoot at a large target set up along the approach <ref name="歩射"/>. Preparations begin on January 2 and proceed through various rituals, forming a traditional rite <ref name="歩射"/>. It is designated a Fukuoka Prefecture intangible folk cultural property as the “Shikaumi Shrine Hosha Festival” <ref name="歩射"/>.  
; Yamahome Tanemaki Gyoryō-sai / Yamahome Gyoryō-sai  
: Also called the “Yamahome Festival.” The spring Yamahome Tanemaki Gyoryō-sai is held on April 15, and the autumn Yamahome Gyoryō-sai on November 15 <ref name="山ほめ"/>. Formerly they were held on lunar February 15 and November 15 and were called the “Hunting and Fishing Festival” <ref name="山ほめ"/>. The spring rite includes gestures of sowing to pray for a good harvest, while the autumn rite includes gestures of hauling nets to pray for a bountiful catch.  
: Next, the three Shika mountains (Katsuyama, Kinugasa-yama, and Mikasa-yama) are purified and praised (yamahome) <ref name="山ほめ"/>. Then gestures of shooting a deer (hunting rite) and catching sea bream (fishing rite) are performed <ref name="山ほめ"/>. It is designated a Fukuoka Prefecture intangible folk cultural property as the “Yamahome Festival” <ref name="山ほめ"/>.  
: As a {{ill|kagura uta|ja|神楽歌|qid=Q11590393}}, the following song is sung <ref>[http://www.sikanosima.jp/event-maturi/yamafome08/index2.html Yamahome Gyoryō Festival] (personal website).</ref>.

of the Azumi lineage).  
; Tanabata Festival  
: A festival held from August 6 to 7 praying for safe fishing and a good catch <ref name="七夕"/>. Formerly it was held on lunar July 7 <ref name="七夕">[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/123 Tanabata Festival of Shikaumi Shrine] (Fukuoka City Economic Tourism and Culture Bureau, “Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City”).</ref>.  
: During the festival, fishermen of Hakata Bay visit the port on boats flying big-catch flags, then worship at Shikaumi Shrine <ref name="七夕"/>. The festival is also mentioned in Kaibara Ekken’s *Chikuzen no Kuni Zoku Fudoki*, and it is said that in earlier times there were many stalls <ref name="七夕"/>.  
; Otokoyama Festival  
: A rite held on October 1 to decide by {{ill|demarchy|bg|Демархия|ca|Demarquia|cs|Demarchie|de|Demarchie|es|Demarquía|eu|Demarkia|fa|دمارشی|fi|Demarkia|hy|Դեմարխիա|ja|くじ|nl|Demarchie|oc|Demarquia|pt|Demarquia|ru|Демархия|sh|Ždrijeb (izbori)|simple|Demarchy|tl|Demarkiya|tr|Demarşi|uk|Демархія|xmf|დემარქია|qid=Q5433694}} whether the year’s grand festival will include a procession <ref name="神幸"/>. Formerly it was held on lunar September 1 <ref name="神幸"/>. However, today the procession is conducted biennially <ref name="神幸"/>.  

== Cultural properties ==
== Important Cultural Property (national designation) ==
* Gilded bell (鍍金鐘) (craft)  
*: A {{ill|Bonshō|ar|بونشو|bn|বোনশো|de|Bonshō|es|Bonshō|fa|بونشو|fr|Bonshō|id|Bonshō|it|Bonshō|ja|梵鐘|ko|범종|pl|Japońskie dzwony, dzwonki i gongi|pt|Bonshō|ru|Бонсё|th|บนโช|zh|佛鐘|qid=Q8192099}} (Korean bell) transmitted at Shikaumi Shrine, retaining traces of gilding (“tokin” meaning plating) on its surface. Though small (height 52.8 cm; mouth diameter 30.5 cm), it is characterized by a relatively large dragon handle at the top. The upper and lower bands bear peony arabesque patterns, and four striking pads with sixteen-petaled lotus designs are placed slightly above the lower band. Four seated Buddha images are cast on the bell body, with two heavenly guardian figures beneath each. The bell is unsigned, but its form resembles the Korean bell at {{ill|Mandara-ji Temple|ja|曼陀羅寺|vi|Chùa Mandara (Nhật Bản)|qid=Q11515245}} in {{ill|Kōnan, Aichi|ar|كونان (آيتشي)|arz|كونان, ايتشى|azb|کونان، آیچی|ce|Конан (Айти)|ceb|Kōnan (lungsod sa Hapon)|ckb|کۆنان، ئایچی|de|Kōnan (Aichi)|es|Kōnan (Aichi)|fa|کونان، آیچی|fi|Kōnan (Aichi)|fr|Kōnan (Aichi)|gl|Kōnan, Aichi|he|קונאן (עיר)|hy|Կոնան (Այչի)|id|Kōnan, Aichi|it|Kōnan (Aichi)|ja|江南市|kk|Конан|ko|고난시 (아이치현)|mg|Kōnan|mzn|کونان، آیچی|nl|Konan (Aichi)|pl|Kōnan (Aichi)|pnb|کونان|pt|Kōnan (Aichi)|ro|Kōnan, Aichi|ru|Конан (Айти)|sv|Kōnan, Aichi|th|โคนัง (จังหวัดไอจิ)|tl|Kōnan, Aichi|tr|Kōnan, Aichi|tt|Конан (Айти)|uk|Конан (Айті)|ur|کؤنان، ایچی|vi|Kōnan, Aichi|war|Kōnan, Aichi|wuu|江南市|zh|江南市|zh_classical|江南市|zh_min_nan|Kônan-chhī|zh_yue|江南市|qid=Q820496}}, which bears a date corresponding to 1234 CE, and it is thought to date to the early 13th century in the {{ill|Goryeo|af|Goryeo|ar|مملكة غوريو|ast|Koryo|az|Qoryo|azb|قوریو|ba|Корё|bg|Корьо|bs|Goryeo|bxr|Корё улас|ca|Goryeo|cdo|Gŏ̤-là̤|ckb|گۆریۆ|cs|Korjo|da|Goryeo|de|Goryeo|es|Koryo|eu|Goryeo|fa|گوریو|fi|Goryeo|fr|Goryeo|hi|गोर्यो|hu|Korjo|id|Dinasti Goryeo|it|Goryeo|ja|高麗|jv|Dinasti Goryeo|ka|კორიო|ko|고려|ku|Goryeo|lt|Gorjo|lv|Korjo dinastija|mk|Корјо|mn|Гуулин улс|ms|Dinasti Goryeo|my|ဂိုလျော|mzn|گوریو|nl|Goryeo|no|Goryeo|pl|Goryeo|ps|گوریو|pt|Goryeo|ro|Dinastia Goryeo|ru|Корё|sh|Goryeo|si|ගොර්යෝ|simple|Goryeo|sk|Korjo|sr|Korjo|sv|Koryo|th|โครยอ|tok|ma Kolijo|tr|Koryo|uk|Корьо|vi|Cao Ly|wuu|高丽王朝|xmf|კორიო|zh|高麗|zh_classical|高麗國|zh_min_nan|Ko-lê|zh_yue|高麗|qid=Q28208}} period <ref name="坪井">Ryohei Tsuboi, *Revised: Bonshō and Ancient Culture* (Business Education Publishing, 1993), pp. 302–304.</ref>. Deposited at the {{ill|Fukuoka City Museum|ff|Fukuoka City Museum|fr|Musée municipal de Fukuoka|id|Museum Kota Fukuoka|ja|福岡市博物館|ko|후쿠오카시 박물관|th|พิพิธภัณฑ์นครฟูกูโอกะ|zh|福岡市博物館|zh_yue|福岡市博物館|qid=Q11592224}}. Designated April 14, 1906 (Meiji 39).  

== Fukuoka Prefecture-designated cultural properties ==
* Tangible cultural properties  
** Stone Hōkyōintō pagoda (archaeological material) <ref name="塔">[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/323 Stone Hōkyōintō Pagoda] (Fukuoka City Economic Tourism and Culture Bureau, “Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City”).</ref> — Designated October 29, 1958 (Shōwa 33).  
** Fragmentary mold for a slender bronze sword (archaeological material)  
**: A casting mold for a {{ill|Slender bronze dagger|ja|細形銅剣|ko|세형동검|zh|細形銅劍|qid=Q12602346}} estimated to date to the early first half of the Middle Yayoi period; excavated in 1947 from the Katsuma area and owned by Shikaumi Shrine <ref name="銅剣">[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/322 Fragmentary Mold for a Slender Bronze Sword] (Fukuoka City Economic Tourism and Culture Bureau, “Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City”).</ref>. The mold is sandstone; both ends are missing, and the remaining length is 18.1 cm <ref name="銅剣"/>. Designated July 26, 1958 (Shōwa 33).  
* Intangible folk cultural properties  
** Shikaumi Shrine Hosha Festival <ref name="歩射">[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/112 Shikaumi Shrine Hosha Festival] (Fukuoka City Economic Tourism and Culture Bureau, “Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City”).</ref> — Designated March 31, 1959 (Shōwa 34).  
** Yamahome Festival <ref name="山ほめ">[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/115 Yamahome Festival] (Fukuoka City Economic Tourism and Culture Bureau, “Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City”).</ref> — Designated January 12, 1960 (Shōwa 35).  
** Shikaumi Shrine Shinkō Event <ref name="神幸">[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/133 Shikaumi Shrine Shinkō Event] (Fukuoka City Economic Tourism and Culture Bureau, “Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City”).</ref> — Designated August 16, 1960 (Shōwa 35).  

== Fukuoka City-designated cultural properties ==
* Tangible cultural properties  
** Illustrated Shikaumi Shrine origin scrolls, 3 hanging scrolls (painting) — Deposited at Fukuoka City Museum. Designated March 7, 1985 (Shōwa 60).  
** Shikaumi Shrine documents, 45 items (books/manuscripts/old texts) — Designated March 7, 1985 (Shōwa 60).  
* Tangible folk cultural property  
** Power stones of Shikaumi Shrine  
**: Edo-period {{ill|Chikaraishi|ar|شيكاريشي|az|Çikaraişi|da|Styrkesten|fr|Chikaraishi|ja|力石|qid=Q1660393}} beside the shrine worship hall <ref name="力石">[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/427 Power Stones of Shikaumi Shrine] (Fukuoka City Economic Tourism and Culture Bureau, “Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City”).</ref>. A natural basalt stone: length 66 cm, width 36 cm, weight 118.2 kg <ref name="力石"/>. Designated March 2006 (Heisei 18).

nienz|zea|1868|zh|1868年|zh_classical|一八六八年|zh_min_nan|1868 nî|zh_yue|1868年|qid=Q7717}}) due to the separation of Shinto and Buddhism <ref name="神々"/>. It is thought that Sōgonji, located south of Shikaumi Shrine, inherited Kisshōji’s lineage <ref name="地名"/>. Sōgonji preserves a Heian-period wooden standing Kannon (Fukuoka City-designated tangible cultural property) and a Nanboku-chō-period bronze seated bodhisattva (also Fukuoka City-designated tangible cultural property).
